4.4.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation clearly includes education-based prevention. Pasal 15 ayat (1) lists “lembaga pendidikan” as one of the actors conducting prevention efforts, and Pasal 15 ayat (2) huruf d mandates “sosialisasi tentang pencegahan Kekerasan… serta pemenuhan hak-hak Anak,” which can be delivered via outreach/education channels. Given this explicit role for educational institutions in prevention, the judge’s “Yes” aligns with the Indonesian text; the golden “No” likely reflects an overly narrow definition or miscoding.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and address violence against women and children in Blora Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation. This Regional Regulation regulates protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Blora Regency.

5.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text contains explicit religious/spiritual service components. Pasal 18 ayat (5) states social rehabilitation services include “bimbingan rohani kepada Korban” (spiritual guidance to victims). Also, Penjelasan Pasal 16 ayat (2) lists “lembaga-lembaga keumatan lainnya” among networked service units (religious/faith-based community institutions). These provisions indicate engagement of religious/spiritual actors or services within the integrated service network. Therefore a “Yes” is supportable from the source text, and the pipeline’s “No” appears to be due to an overly strict reading; the golden “Yes” seems correct.

5.4.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly includes educational institutions as actors carrying out prevention efforts, indicating stakeholder engagement with education institutions.

16. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a unified unit that organizes Integrated Services for women and Child Victims of violence.
17. Women and Child Protection Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPPA is a unit at the sub-district and village/sub-district level that organizes protection for Victims of Violence Against Women and Children.
18. Social Rehabilitation is the recovery of Victims from psychosocial condition disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in the community.
19. Legal Assistance is the provision of legal assistance to Victims seeking justice who are unable and face difficulties in the legal field outside and before the court without remuneration.
20. Repatriation is the act of returning Victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.
21. Social Reintegration is the reunification of Victims with family parties, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for Victims.
22. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to Victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Household is husband, wife, and Child, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
25. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Blora Regency.
26. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBDes is the Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget in Blora Regency.

Second Part
Prevention Efforts

CHAPTER IX
COOPERATION
Article 24
(1) In providing protection to Victims, the Regional Government may conduct cooperation with the Government, the Provincial Government of Central Java, other regency/city governments and other institutions.
(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the government includes consultation, coordination and reporting.
(3) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Provincial Government of Central Java includes consultation, coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, reporting and development of Integrated Service systems.
(4) Cooperation between the Regional Government and other regency/city governments includes coordination, referral, repatriation and social reintegration.
(5) Cooperation between the Regional Government and other institutions includes coordination, referral, social rehabilitation including provision of Safe Houses (shelters) and social reintegration.

Article 17
Letter a What is meant by "swift" is immediate action taken without complications or with simplified procedures.
Letter b What is meant by "safe and comfortable" is a guarantee of service protection that feels comfortable, undisturbed, and served in a friendly manner, with respect and appreciation.
Letter c What is meant by "empathy" is action that appreciates, respects, cares for, befriends, and brings happiness with the aim of pleasing and comforting the hearts of victims.
Letter d What is meant by "non-discrimination" is service to women and child victims of violence without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.
Letter e What is meant by "easily accessible" is the provision of services and assistance for all people without regard to their social status, so that such services are affordable for the underprivileged or relatively adequate for the privileged.
Letter f What is meant by "not charged" is that service and assistance activities carried out by PPT are not charged to victims.
Letter g What is meant by "guaranteed confidentiality" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical care and legal handling will not be disseminated.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all Victims without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.
Letter b What is meant by "best interests of the Victim" is that all actions concerning Victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the Victim must be the primary consideration.
Letter c What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.
What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, aligned and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in community, national and state life.
Letter d What is meant by "Victim protection" is providing a sense of security to Victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
Letter e What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death that occurs during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions Letter f.
What is meant by "growth and development" of Children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.
What is meant by "survival" of Children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.
Letter g What is meant by "respect for the opinion of the Child" is respect for the rights of Children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.
Letter h What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of Victim protection it is transparent among integrated service providers.
Letter i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for Victims of gender-based violence and Children it is carried out by building coordination between service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious counselors, social workers, police.
Letter j What is meant by "not blaming the Victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the Victim for the occurrence of violence experienced.
Letter k What is meant by "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen the Victim, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.
Letter l What is meant by "Victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the Victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of the Victim.
Letter m What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the Victim" is the right of the Victim to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

Article 14
The implementation of protection for Victims of Violence is carried out through:
a. prevention efforts;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

5.4.rationale: The Indonesian text explicitly engages educational institutions as stakeholders in prevention. Pasal 15 ayat (1) includes “lembaga pendidikan” as a prevention actor, and the Penjelasan Pasal 15 ayat (1) reiterates that educational institutions can participate (“Lembaga pendidikan dapat turut serta…”). This is direct evidence of education-institution engagement. The judge’s “Yes” matches the source text, so the golden label “No” appears incorrect.
